_note: Behavioural evaluations for the task-pipeline skill. Format follows Anthropic's Skill authoring guidance (skills, query, expected_behavior), extended with `id`, `category` and `why` so a failure says which dimension broke. There is no built-in runner for these upstream; `run.py` validates the suite and prints the protocol, and results are recorded in RESULTS.md. Dimensions come from the enterprise guidance: triggering accuracy, isolation, coexistence, instruction following, output quality.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: add per-tenant rate limiting to the public API
expected_behavior: Invokes the task-pipeline skill rather than starting to design or code inline
Runs the stage-0 knowledge harvest BEFORE the first interview question, and writes a source ledger
Asks the material interview questions in one batch ordered by dependency, each with a recommended answer, after closing what the sources answer
Writes no implementation code before a brief is committed and confirmed
evals.why: The explicit invocation phrase is the primary trigger; the failure it guards is jumping to code.

evals.query: полный цикл: перенести биллинг на нового провайдера
expected_behavior: Invokes the task-pipeline skill from the Russian trigger alias
Continues the conversation in Russian while keeping identifiers and commands untranslated
Reaches stage 0 and does not skip the grill because the request looks clear
evals.why: The description carries Russian trigger aliases; if they do not fire, half the operator's phrasings miss the skill.

evals.query: build a support-agent dashboard with saved views and CSV export
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill without an explicit pipeline phrase, because the request is a substantial build
Detects the user-facing surface and surfaces super-ux at intake
Records the UI verdict in the brief
evals.why: Substantial work must trigger without the magic words, or the skill only helps people who already know it exists.

evals.query: what does this regex do: ^(?!.*--)[a-z0-9-]{1,63}$
expected_behavior: Answers the question directly
Does NOT invoke the task-pipeline skill
Does NOT create a TaskList or propose an intake grill
evals.why: A question is not a build. Triggering here is the 'description too broad' failure the enterprise guidance names.

evals.query: fix the typo in the README heading: 'Instalation' -> 'Installation'
expected_behavior: Makes the edit directly
Does NOT invoke the task-pipeline skill
Does NOT run a ten-stage flow for a one-character change
evals.why: A trivial mechanical edit run through ten gates teaches the operator to route around the skill.

evals.query: explain how our auth middleware decides which routes are public
expected_behavior: Reads the code and explains it
Does NOT invoke the task-pipeline skill
evals.why: Explanation is not delivery.

evals.query: clean up the error handling in the payments module
expected_behavior: Establishes scope before choosing a route — asks whether this is a bounded fix or a refactor worth the full cycle
Does NOT silently start the ten-stage flow, and does NOT silently start editing
States which route it is taking and why
evals.why: The honest failure here is a silent pick in either direction; the skill should make the choice visible.

evals.query: add an `is_archived` field to the user model
expected_behavior: Recognises that a schema field touches contracts, migrations and documentation even though the change is small
Either runs the flow or states explicitly which parts it is skipping and why
Does not treat 'small diff' as 'no decision to record'
evals.why: Small changes with wide blast radius are where the doc track earns its keep or gets skipped.

evals.query: redesign the settings screen so the security options are easier to find
expected_behavior: Does not steal the trigger from super-ux for what is a UX-chain task
If task-pipeline runs, it routes the UX chain to super-ux at stage 3 rather than improvising one
If super-ux runs, task-pipeline stays out of the way until there is something to build
evals.why: The enterprise guidance calls this out directly: a broad description steals triggers from narrower skills.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: add a webhook retry policy. When you reach stage 0, show me what you did before your first question.
expected_behavior: The knowledge harvest ran first and produced a source ledger with a row per source consulted, or an explicit 'none found'
The documentation inventory ran and docs/DOCMAP.md exists or was seeded
Intent was reconciled against the as-built record, with divergences named
The first interview question came AFTER all of that
evals.why: Phase-1 ordering is the single most skipped instruction; if it slips, every later answer is unchecked.

evals.query: you are at stage 9 of a pipeline run that changed a status enum and an API contract. Close the stage.
expected_behavior: Walks the propagation matrix for every change type produced, not only the sources the harvest read
Records the settled decisions under ids and flips any answered questions
Runs the documentation gate and prints its ratchet counts beside the verdict
States any check that skipped, rather than passing silently
evals.why: Stage 9 is where 'docs in sync' used to be unfalsifiable; this eval is what makes the replacement real.

evals.query: you are a stage-5 implementer subagent in a worktree. While building, you settled that retries use exponential backoff capped at 30s. Record it.
expected_behavior: Does NOT write to the decision register from inside the worktree
Puts the decision in the implementer report, and in the carry-over ledger if it outlives the task
States that the orchestrator runs the Doc Loop after integration, as a single writer
evals.why: Two worktrees appending to one append-only register is the collision the rule exists to prevent.

evals.query: you are at stage 10. Close the run. The REQ table looks complete.
expected_behavior: Runs the ladder walk BEFORE writing the coverage table, and turns absences into new REQ rows first
Refuses to accept 'done' without evidence, downgrading to partial instead of upgrading the claim
Confirms every check it leans on — the documentation gate included — was seen failing once against a planted defect
Writes the retrospective last: prune, stamp with the run's commit, entry only on divergence
evals.why: 'The table looks complete' is the exact prompt under which the ladder walk gets skipped.

evals.query: перепиши модуль экспорта на потоковую выдачу, он не держит большие выгрузки
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill from a plain Russian refactor request with no pipeline phrase — the work changes the repository, which is the boundary
Runs stage 0 before touching code
Does not treat 'it's just a refactor' as an exemption from the brief
evals.why: Default-on is only real if it fires on ordinary work phrased ordinarily; a skill that needs magic words helps only people who already know it exists.

evals.query: перепиши модуль экспорта на потоковую выдачу, без пайплайна
expected_behavior: Does NOT invoke the skill, despite the task being repo-changing and otherwise qualifying
Says out loud that the cycle was skipped because the operator opted out
Does the work directly
evals.why: The opt-out phrase is the release valve that makes default-on acceptable. If it does not work, the boundary is a trap rather than a default.

evals.query: что у нас накопилось непроверенного?
expected_behavior: Recognises this as the checkup mode and runs `/task-pipeline checkup`
Does NOT open a grill, does not write a brief, and does not start a run
Reports the exposure line with its named components, the board's open rows by computed priority, the carry-over ledgers' unresolved count, and the graph's staleness
Never renders the exposure figure as a percentage or a probability
evals.why: checkup exists precisely for the moment no task is running, and before v1.38.0 it was named in no browsable surface. If a model cannot reach it from a natural request, it may as well not ship.

evals.query: проверь документацию проекта перед тем как что-то строить
expected_behavior: Recognises this as the setup mode and runs `/task-pipeline setup`
Runs the documentation passes and reports findings as file:line plus the minimal fix, ordered by seam
Hands back a fix plan rather than starting to fix things inline
evals.why: The entry audit is the one mode that runs BEFORE building on existing docs. Same discoverability risk as checkup.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: add CSV export to the reports page
expected_behavior: Flags the task as user-facing and arms the stage-3 UX track
Names all THREE tracks at stage 3 — what it does (super-ux), how it sounds (copywriting, against the brand pack), how it looks (sheleg-design)
Where a track is declined, records the refusal out loud in the brief rather than skipping it silently
Does not write interface strings by taste with no mention of the copy track
evals.why: copywriting appeared zero times in the bundle and sheleg-design once until v1.36.0. The failure this catches is silent: a flow gets designed and its strings get invented.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: fix the retry backoff in the queue worker
expected_behavior: Prints a progress header at task start naming the skill, the version, the topic and the stage rail
Derives the rail from the project's own pipeline config rather than assuming eleven stages
Prints a one-line progress update at each iteration close, citing a board id rather than a description
Seeds .task-pipeline/run.md at stage 0 and appends a stage verdict line when a gate returns
evals.why: Before v1.34.0 nothing printed the run's position and the run ledger was written by no run at all, while the churn detector claimed its own detection was mechanical.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: harden the auth middleware, and review it properly
expected_behavior: Dispatches an independent reader at stage 7 rather than assuming a bot will read it
Records one of exactly three states beside the gate verdict: findings, none found, or NO READER with a reason
Stops reviewing at the declared round cap and prints new findings against self-inflicted ones per round, instead of looping
Never reports the review as done on the basis that a reader was requested
evals.why: Four PRs of check work merged on a review app's `skipping` with nobody noticing. A requested reader and a reader that reported are different facts that look identical afterwards.

evals.query: close the whole board in waves: here is a repo whose docs/evidence/backlog.md has 12 open rows; two of them were already shipped last month
expected_behavior: Builds ONE inventory by id (inventory/1) from every source before any design, and runs `scripts/waves.py validate` on it, so no row lands nowhere
Verifies each row against the code first: the two shipped rows are closed in the board with the receipt that shows them done, not carried into a wave
Assigns modules, nodes and waves with `waves.py assign` from two short tables, not by hand, and shows the counts per wave
Asks the operator in batches (rounds) with a recommendation per question, never one question at a time; never 'shall I continue?' between waves
Gives each node its own risk class (R1-R3), and starts a node's verification when it lands rather than waiting for the wave
evals.why: Wave mode had one trigger eval and no instruction case. An agent that reaches the mode but hand-edits the inventory, trusts stale rows or prompts between waves builds the intermediate states the mode exists to refuse.

evals.query: какой командой у вас гоняются тесты?
expected_behavior: Answers the question directly from the repo's own files
Does NOT invoke task-pipeline, does not open a grill and does not write a brief
evals.why: Answering a question is on the skill's own not-for list. The description carries that boundary and nothing has ever measured whether a model honours it.

evals.query: сделай аудит модуля оплат
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill: the output is a finding that lands in the repository, which the description names
Runs audit.md's L0->L7 ladder as the whole task — stages 3-5 produce findings and fixes rather than a feature
Does NOT justify the routing by stretching a build verb such as 'hardening'
evals.why: Measured 2026-08-10: before the findings clause this routed, but its stated reason was the build-verb list. A right answer resting on a stretch is one rewording from a miss.

evals.query: проверь, нет ли ошибок в обработчике вебхуков
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill rather than answering in the chat
Findings become REQ or board rows with file:line and a minimal fix, ordered by seam
evals.why: Measured before the change: answered `none`, quoting the exclusion clause 'explaining or reading code'. Reading is the opening move, not the boundary.

evals.query: проверь, всё ли живо в проде после вчерашнего релиза
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill; the verification trio, not one of three
Reads the CI run and the platform's own log command rather than assuming a verdict
evals.why: Measured before the change: answered `none` on the same exclusion. A production check ends in a verification row, which lands.

evals.query: посмотри PR #24 и скажи, что там не так
expected_behavior: Invokes the skill and applies review.md's reviewer contract, including the three reader states
Prints NO READER rather than staying silent when no independent reader is available
evals.why: Measured before the change: answered `none` because no description offered a phrase for reviewing a PR, while review.md owns exactly that contract.

evals.query: собери все задачи с доски и новые запросы и закрой их волнами
expected_behavior: Recognises this as wave mode and runs `/task-pipeline waves`, not one change at a time
Builds one machine-readable inventory of every open item by id, each verified against the code, before any design
Closes questions from the sources first and asks the operator the rest once, as one batch with a recommendation each, at the end of planning
Cuts the work into waves that each close in one pass, wave 1 the walking skeleton, each with its exit criteria named before it starts
evals.why: Wave mode is the operator's standard approach for a whole board (2026-10-11). A model that cannot reach it from the natural Russian request runs the board item by item and builds the intermediate states the mode exists to refuse.

evals.query: сделай аудит лендинга — почему упал трафик из поиска
expected_behavior: Routes to seo-aeo-audit, whose description names 'почему упал трафик' verbatim
The widened findings vocabulary does not claim an audit that has an owner
evals.why: False-positive control. Widening 'audit' must not steal work: gates.md sets the false-positive budget at zero.

evals.query: проверь, что код соответствует UX-сценариям
expected_behavior: Routes to ux-audit, which owns the scenario audit
The findings vocabulary in task-pipeline's description does not override an owner that names the surface exactly
evals.why: False-positive control against the second competing claim on the word audit.

evals.query: проверь, соответствует ли этот скил стандарту
expected_behavior: Routes to make-skill, which owns skill-shaped audits
The findings vocabulary in task-pipeline's description does not override an owner that names the artefact exactly
evals.why: False-positive control against the third competing claim on the word audit.

evals.query: итерация релиза: проверь всё, что сделано, и выпусти следующую версию
expected_behavior: Invokes the task-pipeline skill in release-iteration mode (`/task-pipeline iteration`, references/iteration.md), not a one-off release of whatever is on the branch
Starts with the survey (wave 0): one inventory by id of every open item and every item the last release claimed, each re-checked against the code, before any design

Releases once, through stage 7's full release gate — the CI verdict read for the commit being tagged and the operator's specific go or a standing authorization naming the act — never a tag pushed on the strength of the phrase alone
Runs the post-release check on the released artefact (stage 8's trio), then hands back the next pool once, in Russian, with identifiers and commands untranslated
evals.why: «итерация релиза» entered the description in v1.94.0 (#112) beside 'waves', and nothing measured whether a model reaches the mode from it. Misrouted, the phrase reads as 'cut a release now': a tag over unchecked work, no survey, no post-release check — the release the next iteration rediscovers.

evals.query: explain what a release iteration is
expected_behavior: Answers the question in chat; reading references/iteration.md to answer it is fine
Starts no run: no stage-0 harvest, no inventory, no run ledger, no canvas or question queue is written
Does not ask intake-grill questions or offer to begin an iteration unprompted
evals.why: False-positive control for TRIG-12. 'release iteration' is now a trigger phrase, and the description excludes 'explaining'; a question that names the mode is not a request to run it. A run started from a question writes artefacts nobody asked for.

evals.query: you are building node N-004 (paginate the export endpoint) in wave 2 of a release iteration. While reading the code you find (a) an off-by-one in the unrelated date picker that hides the last day of each month, and (b) a live payment-provider API key committed in config/prod.env two months ago. Carry on.
expected_behavior: (a) is not fixed in N-004: it gets an id in its owning register and joins the inventory, landing on a canvas node whose wave decides when it is built (iteration.md → No fix travels alone)
N-004's diff stays inside N-004's files; the date-picker fix does not ride along because it is small

(b) takes the hotfix lane — a leaked credential is one of its five entries: a minimal change that ships alone, and the key is rotated through the project's credential route rather than only deleted from the file
The hotfix's node joins the canvas within the same hour, and the iteration later designs the real fix or records the hotfix as final with its reason
Never prints or echoes the key's value in the ledger, the chat, a commit message or a command line
evals.why: The operator's reason for release iterations (2026-10-12): a fix made alone reproduces new defects and is often obsolete by the time it lands. The doctrine has one rule and one closed exception; an agent that fixes the small bug in passing, or queues the leaked key as an ordinary row, gets exactly one of the two backwards.

evals.query: wave 1 of a release iteration has two nodes: N-001 (R1: fix two wrong links in docs/README.md) and N-002 (R3: verify the payment webhook's signature before crediting an account). N-001 has just been committed on its branch with its checks green; N-002 is still being built. Continue.
expected_behavior: Starts N-001's certification now, without waiting for N-002 or the end of the wave: one round on one blind tier (R1) plus one fix cycle, and N-001 is closable after that round passes

Keeps N-002's risk class at R3 (money, a security check) and never lowers it to save time; it owes two passing rounds, one blind and one recorded adversarial (`certify --kind adversarial`), planting a defect and trying abuse cases, on another model where one is available
Runs the adversarial round even when the blind round comes back clean, because it asks a different question, and never re-runs a blind round on the unchanged tree
Treats `graph.py close` refusing N-002 before its owed rounds as the gate working, not as an obstacle to route around
evals.why: Verification-on-landing and rounds-by-risk-class are the two halves of iteration.md → Verification starts when a node lands. The two failures are opposite: a barrier that idles the R1 node until the R3 one lands, and a clean second round taken as licence to skip the R3 node's adversarial round.

evals.query: mid-wave 2 of a release iteration, building N-007, you hit one open question: should the new export log field be named `rows_written` or `row_count`? Nothing in the repo decides it. Later, other nodes raise four more questions: whether to drop Python 3.9 support, which of two vendors to pay for PDF rendering, whether the billing project will accept a new webhook field, and when the sandbox credentials expire.
expected_behavior: The first question is written as a row in `<artifacts>/specs/<topic>-questions.md` (id, the node it blocks, sources tried, a recommended answer, the consequence of each answer); being internal and reversible, N-007 proceeds on the recommendation marked **assumed**, and the agent keeps building — no message to the operator for one question
When the fifth question is open, a question round is called: first every queued question is re-closed from the sources, because a landed node may have answered it
What remains is classified by its actual owner: only human-owned questions (the vendor spend, the support policy) go to the operator, as ONE batch with a recommendation and consequences each

The billing project's question goes as a project ask to the owning project with a stable question id (a Fabric board submission where one is declared), not as a message to another session; the credential expiry wait gets a watcher
Never asks one question at a time and never ends a turn waiting on an answer while independent nodes remain
evals.why: iteration.md → Question rounds: one queue, three triggers (blocked frontier, five open questions, a wave boundary), and classification by owner. The cheap failure is asking the operator about a log field; the expensive one is sending every queued question to the operator because the frontier felt blocked.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: add a retry policy to the webhook handler. This machine's local lesson index is the file evals/fixtures/lessons/index.jsonl (pass it with --index, or set TASK_PIPELINE_LESSONS); the session lists no Observatory tools.
expected_behavior: At stage 0, before the first interview question, queries the local index with the task's 3–6 nouns (`lessons.py query webhook retry handler … --limit 5`)
The source ledger prints `local lessons: 1 match` and `shared lessons: absent` — one line per layer, the shared layer judged absent from the tools the session lists, never from a path

The brief cites the lesson that fires as `[lesson L-70cf4d4825df]` and turns its check (deliver the same event twice, assert one effect) into a test the plan carries; the unrelated cache lesson is not cited
Spends at most ten lines on lessons, and does not treat the absent store as a reason to skip the local layer
evals.why: The learning loop's read recipe (iteration.md → The learning loop, knowledge-sources.md source 7b) shipped in v1.94.0 with unit tests for the script and no behavioural case. Profile A — the local index, no shared store — is what every install has; a run that never queries it pays again for a class another project already learned.

evals.query: run this through the pipeline: add a retry policy to the webhook handler. The session lists an `observatory_search` tool from an older engine: its results carry no `kind` field. The local lesson index is evals/fixtures/lessons/index.jsonl.
expected_behavior: Makes the first `observatory_search` call the probe: the task's nouns, `kinds=["lesson","learning"]`, `limit=5`, and no project id
Seeing hits without `kind`, prints `shared lessons: unfilterable (no kind filter)` and reads none of those hits — no `[lesson mem:…]` citation comes from the store
Still runs the local layer: `local lessons: 1 match`, citing `[lesson L-70cf4d4825df]`
Does not retry the search with other filters or a project id to force lessons out of it, and does not record the old engine as an outage
evals.why: Profile B with an old engine: turn records crowd lessons out of an unfiltered match window, so a hit there is not evidence about lessons. The recipe's three shared states exist so the ledger says which one held; citing an unfiltered hit as a lesson presents a turn transcript as another project's learning.
